hook: The country with the most nuclear weapons isn't America. It's Russia.
twist: SIPRI's January 2026 estimate: Russia 5,420 warheads, the US 5,042; then a cliff to China's 620, which is growing faster than anyone's. Nine countries hold about 12,187 between them, and Russia and the US hold about 83% of the usable ones.
angle: Countdown of all nine nuclear-armed states from SIPRI Yearbook 2026 (Table 8A.1), ending on the near-tie at the top and the gap below it. One big number: 5,420.
why_now: Data: SIPRI Yearbook 2026 (June 2026) is the newest edition; New START expired in February 2026. Demand: YouTube search 'countries with the most nuclear weapons' (2026-10-07, Shorts since 2024-06): top 51.4M, median of top 25 13.3M; the 2026-10-06 scout found 'Top 10 Countries with the Most Nuclear Weapons in 2025' at 14.9M views on a 181k-sub channel (outlier 82) and 'Top 10 Nuclear Powers 2025' at 7.1M.
risks: All counts are SIPRI estimates (secret arsenals): label 'SIPRI estimates' on screen.
Total inventory includes retired warheads awaiting dismantlement; say 'warheads' and name the measure on screen (total inventory).
Serious subject: keep the deadpan dry, no jokes about use.
